title: Equalize Strings by Adding or Removing Characters at Ends
summary: Determine the minimum number of operations required to transform the string initial into the string target by adding or removing exactly one character at either the beginning or the end of initial in each operation.
statement: Determine the minimum number of operations required to transform the string initial into the string target by adding or removing exactly one character at either the beginning or the end of initial in each operation.
constraints: initial and target are strings and may be empty.
One operation adds or removes one character at either end of the current string.
Return the minimum operations required to transform initial into target.
hints: Characters not removed from the original must form one contiguous block, and the same block must be the contiguous portion retained in the target.
Find the longest common substring; remove everything around it from initial and add everything around it for target.
Use rolling DP where equal characters extend the previous diagonal; answer=m+n-2*longest.
Any transformation preserves at most one contiguous middle block, and retaining the longest such block saves exactly two operations per character.
editorial: Any transformation preserves at most one contiguous middle block, and retaining the longest such block saves exactly two operations per character.

tests.explanation: Keep the common contiguous block cde, remove ab, and add f, totaling three operations.
No nonempty block can remain in place, so remove three characters and add three, totaling six.
